about: The minimum buy-in belongs to the table (redesign RD-16; owner, 15 Nov). When an admin adds a table, or gives a table another stake, Tables setup suggests 50 big blinds of the stake; the admin may type another amount. A minimum buy-in is above zero, a whole ₹50 as every buy-in on the floor is, and has no maximum, so there is no cap to reach. Blinds are whole 50s, so 50 of them are a whole ₹50 already and nothing is rounded. The database computes nothing here: it stores the amount the admin saves and refuses one that is not a whole ₹50 above zero.

cases.description: Blinds of 50/150, a big blind that is not a round hundred: 50 of them are still whole 50s, so nothing is rounded.
A straddle does not count: 100/200/500 is suggested from its big blind of ₹200.
No cap: a big game of 5,000/10,000.
A big blind of nothing suggests nothing, which no table may then keep.
₹10,000 may be a table's minimum buy-in.
An amount other than the suggestion may be: ₹7,350 at 100/200.
The least there can be: one ₹50.
₹7,349 is a rupee short of a whole ₹50, so it may not be.
